proof_scope: In progress. R1758 proves the first analytic reduction of continuous expansion for the actual augmented rational family. Its identity and legal opposite translations preserve the original set and shifted cell parts. The measure gain is at least the absolute difference of the occupied measures of two adjacent grid cells. The grid partition covers every unit-interval set up to a finite null boundary, and its cell masses sum exactly to the set measure. A finite path-and-average argument therefore proves that expansion at most 1+sigma implies |K*m_i-M| <= K*(K-1)*sigma*M for every cell, where M=volume(A), m_i=volume(A intersect cell_i), K>=2 and sigma>=0. An explicit expansion-or-uniformity dichotomy follows. No half-measure restriction is required for this intermediate reduction. The K*(K-1) factor is a routine sharpening of the source K^2 estimate, not a novelty claim or an unconditional expansion proof.
